source.title: Stepping on the Edge: Curvature Aware Learning Rate Tuners
source.authors: Vincent Roulet; Atish Agarwala; Jean-Bastien Grill; Grzegorz Swirszcz; M. Blondel; F. Pedregosa

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports experiments on learning-rate tuning, training loss, sharpness, and the learning-rate–sharpness product, using those measures to examine behavior near and above the edge of stability.
record.gate_note: Results about train loss and curvature dynamics bear on V5. CIFAR-10 experiments use subsets for full-batch runs and squared loss; the paper does not report training classification error, random-label results, or the CIFAR-100 result described by V1. Results cited from prior work are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study's constant-learning-rate, full-batch GD controls measure training loss and Hessian sharpness, directly bearing on V5's edge-of-stability component. Comparisons of tuner performance alone do not test V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors argue that greedy tuners can suppress stabilizing curvature feedback and slow full-batch training. CDAT can improve on tuned constant rates and produce automatic warm-up behavior, but prefixed schedules can outperform it, stochastic results are mixed, and the theoretical model only partially explains its stability.
record.recipe_differences: Studies adaptive learning-rate tuners and curvature feedback rather than the specific learning-rate-above-initial-linearized-stability-limit recipe in V5. It uses CDAT, linesearch, and quadratically greedy rules across several optimizers and settings.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with full-batch versus mini-batch training, CDAT scaling factor, batch size, EMA, optimizer, and architecture; CDAT at higher scales can diverge, and schedules can outperform CDAT.

fits_no_version.finding: Classical tuners undershoot the edge, progressively sharpen and underperform constant-rate training; CDAT deliberately targeting the edge can improve training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive learning-rate rules alter curvature feedback, and greedy one-step loss reduction can impair long-term optimization.

fits_no_version.finding: CDAT's favorable scaling depends on batch size and EMA, and its performance relative to scheduled training varies.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Curvature-based learning-rate tuning requires different scaling and estimation choices in stochastic training.

record.problems: Results bearing on V5 are largely qualitative descriptions of plotted curves; exact endpoint values and uncertainty estimates are not stated. The CIFAR-10 full-batch experiments use subsets, and the paper does not test the specific initialization-stability-limit setup in V5.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows were omitted. Figure-only values were not reconstructed.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks, including random labels; model-size, regularization and early-stopping qualifications.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and the effect of adding student neurons.
Training degradation with depth and its prevention by identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Activation-matched initialization, signal propagation, training speed and trainable depth.

Recovery after a brief loss rise above the initial linearized stability limit; divergence at larger fixed rates; divergence despite initially subthreshold rates. CDAT scale sweeps do not establish these components.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

missing.what: A separate constant-rate MixerTi/8 GD control row pairing decreasing training loss with sharpness stabilization and learning-rate–sharpness behavior.

record.verdict_notes: Adaptive-tuner failures do not challenge V5's constant-rate edge-of-stability component. The record incorrectly treats batch-size dependence and relative tuner performance as limits on that claim. No exact plot endpoints were inferred.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not report training classification error, corrupted or random labels, or comparisons of model size and early stopping.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment or width comparison of the stated kind.
No comparison of plain and residual networks by depth and training error. ResNet34 experiments remove batch normalization, but do not test the version's depth and shortcut claim.
No comparison of initializations or signal propagation across depth.

The paper does not test the specific above-initial-linearized-model stability-limit recovery setup or the longer full-batch sharpness behavior attributed to Cohen et al. It studies adaptive rates relative to a local quadratic estimate of the edge, including settings targeted slightly above it.
No batch-normalization comparison of training speed or learning-rate tolerance; the ResNet34 runs omit batch normalization.

rows.subject: ResNet34
rows.operation_detail: Compared tuned constant-rate gradient descent with linesearch and quadratically greedy learning-rate tuning.
rows.baseline: Tuned constant learning rate gradient descent
rows.value: Linesearch and quadratically greedy gradient descent qualitatively underperform the constant-rate counterpart; linesearch may perform better early but stalls in the long term.
rows.note: The paper gives a qualitative comparison, not endpoint training-loss values in text.
rows.check: Relative training-loss performance of learning-rate tuners does not establish recovery above an initial stability limit or sharpness stabilization. This is a method-performance comparison; retain the constant-GD loss trajectory alongside its curvature measurements instead.

rows.subject: ResNet34
rows.operation_detail: Measured learning rate, Hessian sharpness, their product, and gradient norm during constant-rate gradient descent, linesearch, and quadratically greedy tuning.
rows.measure: Learning-rate–sharpness product relative to the edge-of-stability threshold of 2
rows.baseline: Constant-rate gradient descent eventually stabilizes around the threshold of 2.
rows.value: For the tuners, the product neither surpasses the threshold nor stabilizes around 2 in the long run; it stabilizes below the threshold.
rows.note: The paper describes the product and sharpness dynamics qualitatively; plotted values are not transcribed.
rows.check: The relevant evidence is the constant-GD control, currently relegated to the baseline: its learning-rate–sharpness product crosses 2 and subsequently stabilizes below it while training progresses. Separate this from the adaptive tuners, whose below-threshold operation is not an incomplete instance of V5.

rows.subject: ResNet34 with CDAT
rows.operation_detail: Applied CDAT at the listed scaling factors with gradient descent.
rows.value: Scale 1.0 (greedy) underperforms; scales around 2 generally perform better than the constant-rate counterpart; scale 2.5 generally gives diverging results in the short or long term.
rows.note: The text groups scales around the edge and does not state a separate numeric endpoint for each listed scale. Scale 2.06 is specified as 2.0625 in the prose; figure labels round it.
rows.check: This combines several deliberately selected CDAT scales and a method-performance comparison. Scale is not the learning rate divided by the initial linearized stability limit. Neither successful training near scale 2 nor divergence at 2.5 establishes V5's specified recovery dynamics.

rows.subject: ResNet34 with CDAT
rows.operation_detail: Measured sharpness, learning-rate–sharpness product, and gradient norm during CDAT training.
rows.value: Sharpness does not increase and actually decreases slightly over time; CDAT may operate constantly slightly above the edge.
rows.note: The paper reports a slight decrease and operation near/slightly above the edge, not a claim of loss recovery after a brief rise.
rows.check: CDAT deliberately targets the edge through adaptive learning rates. Its decreasing sharpness does not test spontaneous sharpening and stabilization under constant-rate GD or recovery after an initial loss rise.

rows.subject: ResNet50 with squared loss SGD Mom on Cifar10
rows.operation_detail: Swept CDAT scaling factor across batch sizes and EMA settings.
rows.measure: Average end training loss divided by initial training loss
rows.value: The optimal scaling decreases as batch size decreases; EMA smooths performance across batch sizes. The figure shows values but the text gives no exact numerical outcomes.
rows.note: Extracted only the stated qualitative result; figure values are not read from the plot.
rows.check: Optimal CDAT scaling and its dependence on batch size measure tuner performance, without establishing the stability-limit dynamics V5 names. ResNet50 uses layer normalization in place of batch normalization.

rows.subject: ResNet50 with squared loss SGD Mom on Cifar10
rows.operation_detail: Compared CDAT with constant and scheduled learning rates.
rows.measure: Training loss, test error, and learning rate
rows.baseline: Fine-tuned constant-rate and scheduled SGD with momentum
rows.value: CDAT may outperform the constant-rate counterpart, particularly for large batch sizes, while performing on par with or underperforming scheduled learning rates.
rows.note: The text gives a qualified summary across batch sizes without separate numerical values.
rows.check: This combines training loss, test error and learning rate across batch sizes in a method-performance comparison. It does not measure V5's recovery or full-batch sharpness dynamics. ResNet50 uses layer normalization.

relationships.condition: Constant-rate full-batch GD, ResNet34 without batch normalization, squared loss on 4096 CIFAR-10 examples
relationships.reason: R2's constant-GD control shows sharpness stabilization after crossing the threshold; Figure 1 supplies the accompanying decreasing training loss.
relationships.display_finding: Sharpness stabilized after crossing the stability threshold while training loss decreased.

relationships.condition: Constant-rate full-batch GD, MixerTi/8, squared loss on a CIFAR-10 subset
relationships.reason: Text beyond the recorded rows reports sharpness stabilization for the constant-rate control in Figure 12, alongside decreasing loss in Figure 1; the missing control trajectory should be extracted.
relationships.display_finding: The constant-rate control exhibited sharpness stabilization alongside decreasing loss.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Full-batch ResNet34 on a CIFAR-10 subset with squared loss
reader_labels.reason: Classical tuners undershoot the edge and underperform the constant-rate baseline (R1–R2); CDAT near the edge can perform better, while a higher scale can diverge (R3–R4). This paper does not test the version's specific initial-linearized-model recovery setup.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: CDAT's favorable scale depends on batch size, and its performance can be on par with or worse than scheduled learning rates (R5–R6).
